checker: Claude, in a separate verification pass after drafting. Not a human check, and done by the same model that drafted the text; the editor's review remains the independent one.
method: Each noted sentence was compared with the full text of every source it cites: 34 sources from downloaded originals (Federal Register PDFs, court opinions, statistical releases, datasets), 20 from fetched pages, and 6 sites that block scripted access (Canada Finance x2, Mexican Presidency x3, EFTA) through quoted web extracts. Exact wording, figures, dates and attributions were confirmed by targeted searches of the cached texts. A script then confirmed that every number in a noted sentence appears in the recorded findings.
result: All 97 noted sentences are supported as now worded. Fourteen changes were made: two factual corrections, seven narrowed or corrected wordings, and five notes given additional or better sources.

corrections.was: Switzerland's rate rose to 39 per cent and Laos and Myanmar's to 40
corrections.problem: Laos and Myanmar fell to 40 per cent, from 48 and 44 in the April annex; only Switzerland rose.
corrections.now: Switzerland's rate rose from 31 to 39 per cent, while Laos and Myanmar came down to 40 from 48 and 44

corrections.was: When the global steel and aluminium tariffs took effect on 12 March
corrections.problem: The steel proclamation sets 12 March; no cited source dates the aluminium increase.
corrections.now: When the global steel tariff took effect on 12 March

corrections.was: aluminium was raised to 25 per cent the same day
corrections.problem: The steel proclamation does not cover aluminium.
corrections.now: a companion proclamation raised aluminium to 25 per cent (now citing Proclamation 10947's recital of Proclamation 10895)

corrections.problem: The source shows only that the announcement contained none.

corrections.was: Canada obtained its own pause the same day, and both were formalised in orders dated 3 February.
corrections.problem: Supported only by titles listed in a later order.
corrections.now: Cites Executive Order 14197 itself, which paused the Canadian tariffs until 4 March.

corrections.was: When they ended in early March, ... took effect on 4 March.
corrections.problem: Imprecise; the pause's end date is now sourced.
corrections.now: When the Canadian pause ended on 4 March, ... took effect the same day.

corrections.was: Mexican goods within the agreement would pay nothing.
corrections.problem: The release limits this to 2 April.

corrections.was: including on foreign-made products containing Chinese material and on rare-earth technologies
corrections.problem: Scope taken from secondary summaries; the technology controls proper are a separate announcement not opened.
corrections.now: Scope stated from Announcement No. 61: licences for goods made abroad containing Chinese rare-earth material worth 0.1 per cent of their value, or made with Chinese rare-earth technology.

corrections.was: Japan's agreement, put into effect on 4 September
corrections.problem: 4 September is the date of the implementing order; the tariff terms were backdated to 7 August.
corrections.now: implemented by an order of 4 September and backdated to 7 August

corrections.was: The ruling changed nothing at the border.
corrections.now: In practice the ruling changed nothing at the border.

corrections.was: Even Mexico, which had refused to retaliate against the United States
corrections.now: Even Mexico, which had answered American tariffs by negotiating

corrections.was: de minimis note cited the Canada order only
corrections.problem: The sentence covers all three February orders.
corrections.now: Also cites the Mexico and China orders, Sec. 2(g).

corrections.was: after a call with President Trump (31 July)
corrections.problem: The call was not in the recorded findings.
corrections.now: Recorded from the Presidency release, which attributes the agreement to a telephone conversation.

corrections.was: Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962; joint statement of 12 May
corrections.problem: Statute name and statement date were not in the recorded findings.
corrections.now: Recorded from Proclamation 10896 and the Geneva joint statement.

not_checked: Claims in the opening thesis and in transitional sentences without notes are the author's argument and are not verified as facts. No source was found for the effective date of the March increase of the China fentanyl duty; Figure 2 places it at the order's date and says so.
